stem: In how many ways can all the letters of the word JOURNAL be arranged so that the three vowels (O, U, A) always appear together as a group?

per_option_rationale.rationale: JOURNAL has vowels O, U, A and consonants J, R, N, L. Treating vowels as 1 block gives 5 units. Arrangements of 5 units: 5! = 120. Vowels within the block: 3! = 6. Total = 120 x 6 = 720.
Computed 5! x 3! x 3 = 120 x 6 x 3 = 2160, incorrectly multiplying by an extra factor of 3, perhaps double-counting the block position choices.
Computed only 5! = 120, correctly reducing n but forgetting to multiply by 3! for the internal arrangements of the 3 vowels within the block.
Computed 7! = 5040, the total unrestricted arrangements, ignoring that vowels must stay together.

explanation: JOURNAL has 7 letters: vowels O, U, A and consonants J, R, N, L. Bundle the 3 vowels into one block to get 5 objects. Arrange these 5 objects in a row: 5! = 120 ways. Within the vowel block, the 3 vowels can be in any of 3! = 6 orders. Total = 120 x 6 = 720.

explanation_sections.punchline: Bundle the vowels into one block, count arrangements of the resulting 5 objects, then restore vowel order within the block.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify: linear arrangement, group-together restriction. Step 1 - merge 3 vowels: n reduces from 7 to 5. Step 2 - arrangements of 5 units: 5! = 120. Step 3 - internal vowel arrangements: 3! = 6. Total: 120 x 6 = 720.
explanation_sections.lesson: Group-together restriction: merge the group, compute (new n)!, multiply by (group size)!.
explanation_sections.timing: 30 seconds: 5! x 3! = 120 x 6 = 720. Trap: computing 5! = 120 and forgetting the 3! inside the vowel group.
